comparisons.peer_summary: AMD faces potential intellectual property infringement claims from third parties that could result in substantial damages, injunctions stopping product sales, or costly licensing and redesign efforts, any of which could have a material adverse effect on the business.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose risks related to third-party intellectual property infringement claims and the associated potential for costly licensing or legal outcomes. MU specifically highlights the risk of 'failure to obtain or renew license agreements covering such intellectual property,' while AMD mirrors this by noting that if claims are asserted, it 'may seek to obtain a license,' though it 'cannot assure you that we will be able to obtain all of the necessary licenses on satisfactory terms, if at all.' Both companies acknowledge the threat of litigation leading to damages or injunctions, with AMD explicitly mentioning injunctions against product sales.

sentences.text: • claims that our products or manufacturing processes infringe or otherwise violate the intellectual property rights of others or failure to obtain or renew license agreements covering such intellectual property.

With respect to intellectual property litigation, from time to time, we have been notified of, or third parties may bring or have brought, actions against us and/or against our customers based on allegations that we are infringing the intellectual property rights of others, contributing to or inducing the infringement of the intellectual property rights of others, improperly claiming ownership of intellectual property or otherwise improperly using the intellectual property of others.
We cannot assure you that we will be able to obtain all of the necessary licenses on satisfactory terms, if at all.

These parties may file lawsuits against us or our customers seeking damages (potentially up to and including treble damages) or an injunction against the sale of products that incorporate allegedly infringed intellectual property or against the operation of our business as presently conducted, which could result in our having to stop the sale of some of our products or to increase the costs of selling some of our products or which could damage our reputation.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces warranty claims, product recalls, and product liability, with potential liabilities that may be significant, unlimited, and exceed revenue from relevant products. Reserves and insurance may be inadequate to cover uninsured portions of such claims, materially affecting financial condition.
comparisons.comparison: While AVGO's primary topic in D071 is warranty and product liability, it contains a specific comparable disclosure within that section regarding intellectual property licensing risks. AVGO states, 'In addition, from time to time, we obtain or renew IP licenses. Our inability to obtain or renew these licenses on acceptable terms, or at all, could have a material adverse effect on our business.' This directly parallels MU’s specific risk of 'failure to obtain or renew license agreements covering such intellectual property.' Although AVGO bundles this with warranty risks, the substantive IP licensing content is comparable to MU's focused IP litigation risk.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intellectual Property Litigation Risks and Consequences
comparisons.peer_summary: Third parties, including non-practicing entities, assert IP claims against Intel, which can increase costs, disrupt operations, and harm reputation. Specific examples include an injunction obtained by R2 Semiconductor in Germany in February 2024 and adverse judgments in VLSI and R2 cases. IP claims may require Intel to pay damages, indemnify customers, stop manufacturing products, or enter costly license agreements, potentially harming its competitive position and requiring asset impairments.
comparisons.comparison: MU and INTC both identify the risk that third parties assert intellectual property claims against their products or manufacturing processes. MU's disclosure warns of 'claims that our products or manufacturing processes infringe or otherwise violate the intellectual property rights of others.' Similarly, INTC states that 'third parties assert claims based on IP rights against us and our products' and that 'claims that our products, technologies, or processes infringe the IP rights of others... cause us to incur large costs.' Both companies highlight the financial and operational burden of defending against these claims.

sentences.text: • claims that our products or manufacturing processes infringe or otherwise violate the intellectual property rights of others or failure to obtain or renew license agreements covering such intellectual property.
Third parties assert claims based on IP rights against us and our products, which could harm our business.

Claims that our products, technologies, or processes infringe the IP rights of others, regardless of their merits, cause us to incur large costs to respond to, defend, and resolve the claims, and they divert the efforts and attention of our management and technical personnel from our business and operations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks from IP protection and litigation costs
comparisons.peer_summary: Protecting IP rights and responding to infringement claims may result in substantial costs, damages, or discontinued product sales, and indemnifying customers may negatively impact operating results.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA disclose risks concerning third-party intellectual property infringement claims and the resulting need for licensing. MU warns of 'failure to obtain or renew license agreements covering such intellectual property.' NVDA similarly notes that if infringement claims are made, the company 'may have to seek a license to the third party's IP rights' and that an inability to obtain such a license on acceptable terms could lead to 'substantial liabilities' or suspension of product sales. Both disclosures link infringement claims directly to potential licensing obligations and financial penalties.

sentences.text: • claims that our products or manufacturing processes infringe or otherwise violate the intellectual property rights of others or failure to obtain or renew license agreements covering such intellectual property.

Claims that our products or processes infringe the IP rights of others, regardless of their merit, could cause us to incur significant costs to respond to, defend, and resolve such claims, and they may also divert the efforts and attention of management and technical personnel.
If infringement claims are made against us or our products are found to infringe a third party's IP, we or one of our indemnitees may have to seek a license to the third party's IP rights.

If we or one of our indemnitees is unable to obtain such a license on acceptable terms or at all, we could be subject to substantial liabilities or have to suspend or discontinue the manufacture and sale of one or more of our products.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks of third-party IP infringement claims against Qualcomm
comparisons.peer_summary: Companies may assert patent, copyright, trademark, or other IP claims against Qualcomm, potentially resulting in costly litigation, injunctions, product redesigns, or required licensing and damages. If Qualcomm cannot redesign or license the infringing IP, it could be prohibited from making and selling its products, and suppliers could also be enjoined.
comparisons.comparison: MU and QCOM both address the risk of third-party intellectual property claims that could necessitate licensing, product redesigns, or result in injunctions. MU’s risk factor includes 'claims that our products or manufacturing processes infringe... or failure to obtain or renew license agreements.' QCOM explicitly states that if products are found to infringe IP, the company could be 'required to redesign our products, or to license such intellectual property or pay damages,' and if unable to license, it could be 'prohibited from making and selling our products.' Both companies recognize the severity of potential licensing failures and injunctions stemming from infringement claims.

sentences.text: • claims that our products or manufacturing processes infringe or otherwise violate the intellectual property rights of others or failure to obtain or renew license agreements covering such intellectual property.

From time to time, companies have asserted, and may again assert, patent, copyright, trademark or other intellectual property claims against us relating to our technologies or products, including those we have acquired from other companies.

If any of our products were found to infringe another company's intellectual property, we could be subject to an injunction or be required to redesign our products, or to license such intellectual property or pay damages or other compensation to such other company (any of which could be costly).

If we are unable to redesign our products, license such intellectual property used in our products or otherwise distribute our products (e.g., through a licensed supplier), we could be prohibited from making and selling our products.
